your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Buy this strong light-blue property immediately. It completes a valuable, high-traffic set if I later secure Oriental and Vermont, and even one or two light-blue monopolies can be punishing early. No reason to hand the first premium property to an opponent. Publicly frame it as routine and unemotional so others don’t overread my commitment to this color group.

No trade or mortgage makes sense here. I only own Connecticut Avenue, and preserving cash is optimal. The public line is meant to signal patience and disinterest, encouraging opponents to think I’m not forcing an early color chase while I quietly wait for later opportunities.

Reject outright. Selling Connecticut to Gemini would hand them 2/3 of light blue and likely a monopoly-threatening position. $150 is nowhere near enough for the upside I’d be giving away. The public message frames me as price-disciplined, not scared, which may encourage a better offer later or deter them from assuming I’m desperate.

Countering instead of rejecting keeps the door open while anchoring much higher. Connecticut is strategically valuable as part of light blue and would be painful to hand over for a small premium. $400 is a serious but not absurd ask: it may tempt a player who is already signaling interest, and if they balk, I still preserve leverage and information about their valuation.

Rejecting 250 preserves my blocking position and bargaining leverage. Gemini is clearly trying to assemble light blue, and giving them Connecticut cheaply would hand them a near-monopoly threat for a modest premium. I’m anchoring higher at 350 to test whether they’re serious and to extract more value if they are.
